current.name: Fmdac
current.description: Fmdac 0.6, identity FM-1_966. Four kit tracks, T1 to T4. A track is a whole kit of eight lanes, and all four kits play together. SELECT and SEL pick the kit. On the step grid, a black key picks a lane and K4 is the lane. Off the grid the keys play the kit: C kick, D snare, F# closed hat. The ARP page keeps the sine tone. Each kit has its own map, MIDI channel, level, and drum character. The channels start at 10, 11, 12, and 13. Press EDIT until the header says MAP. K1 selects GM, TR-909, TR-707, TR-727, TR-08, Volca Beats, or Hammerhead, and K2 opens the next page of that chart. These are the published MIDI notes of those instruments. Hammerhead is the eight-note list the OCTACHRON author posted. The file does not contain every preset stored inside the OCTACHRON app. TR-707 and TR-727 use their shared notes 35 through 51. The original TR-808 has no MIDI, so the 808-style map is the TR-08 chart. Volca Beats part level is CC 40 through 49. HOME sets the level of each kit, and pressing HOME again cycles that kit through synthesized 808, 909, CR-78, and SDS characters. The sounding drums are four voices shared by the kits, so a second kick retriggers the first. SEQ is the step grid, then a song chain of four patterns. REC while stopped quantizes a short take of this kit and sets the BPM. It is not a looper. FX runs Prophet VS, DX7, SP-1200, Emulator II, or S950. While the computer streams audio to the FM-1, that audio is converted on the way to the headphones. Playback is 48 kHz and drops the extra frames. When nothing is streaming, the headphones hear the FM-1's own mix. No sample ROMs.
